11784 Chem. Commun., 2012, 48, 11784–11786 This journal is c The Royal Society of Chemistry 2012
Cite this: Chem. Commun., 2012, 48, 11784–11786
Lewis acid-catalyzed unexpected selective C–C bond cleavage: an
eﬃcient and mild construction of cyclopentenes w
Qiong Yu a and Shengming Ma* ab
Received 13th September 2012, Accepted 14th October 2012
DOI: 10.1039/c2cc36672j
An intriguing Lewis acid-catalyzed intramolecular ring-opening/
cyclization reaction of cyclopropylvinylallenes is developed. This
process proceeds at ambient temperature to aﬀord the structurally
diverse cyclopentenes exclusively, which demonstrates the unique
reactivity of 1,3,4-alkatrien-2-yl cyclopropanes.
Selective cleavage of C–C bonds an d subsequent incorporation
into construction of complex molecules represents a fundamental
challenge in organic chemistry. Carbon–carbon bonds in cyclo-
propanes are generally much more reactive because of their
unique strained three-membered carbocyclic structure,
1 therefore,
they play a crucial role as unique units in modern synthetic
chemistry and have attracted the interest of organic chemists for
many years.
1b–e,2 Lewis acid (LA) promoted [3 + n] annulations
of donor–acceptor cyclopropanes have received considerable
attention in recent years: a variety of hetero- or carbocyclic
products have been constructed.
3–8 The Lewis acid-catalyzed
intramolecular [3 + 2] cycloadditions of cyclopropanyl
1,1-dicarboxylate are less prevalent than an intermolecular variant
despite the potential in the synthesis of natural products. Snider
et al. reported a preliminary result on an intramolecular [3 + 2]
cycloaddition of a cyclopropane 1,1-diester with a CQC bond.
9a
Recently, Kerr et al. reported an intramolecular [3 + 2] cyclo-
addition of a cyclopropane 1,1-diester with a C QN bond by
which aza-[3.3.0] and aza-[4.3.0] skeletons were constructed;9b,c
these reactions have been successfully applied to the total synthesis
of FR901483 and allosecurinine.9e,f Wang et al. reported their
results on the construction of the bridged oxa- and aza-[n.2.1] (n =
2, 3, 4) skeletons through intramolecular [3 + 2] cycloaddition of
cyclopropane 1,1-diester.
9d
On the other hand, allenes are a class of compounds of
current interest with unique reactivity. During the last few
decades, allenes have been recognized as a class of very useful
compounds for organic synthesis.
10,11 To the best of our
knowledge, the chemistry of a combination of allenyl and
cyclopropane functionalities has not been reported even though
it may be of great interest in organic synthesis. Recently, our
group has disclosed an eﬃcient method for the synthesis of
allenes with a cyclopropylvinyl substituent.
12 This reaction
proceeds smoothly under neutral conditions, with the exclusive
formation of 1,3,4-alkatrien-2-yl cyclopropane derivatives.
Due to the unique structure of 1, we envisioned that the
cyclopropanyl carboxylate moiety in 1 should undergo ring-
opening to form intermediate M1 with the assistance of Lewis
acids and nucleophiles. Due to the presence of a vicinal
vinylallene substituent, the intermediate M1 should further
undergo cyclization to form the cyclohexene product 2
(Scheme 1). As continuous eﬀort on the allene chemistry, we
report our recent results on the unexpected Zn(OTf)
2-catalyzed
ring-opening/cyclization reaction of cyclopropyl vinylallenes.
To test our hypothesis, we started the initial investigation on
the reaction of 1,1-bis(methoxycarbonyl)-2-hexyl-2-(5 0-ethyl-
10,30,40-heptatrien-20-yl)cyclopropane 1a with 1.2 equiv. of
TMSCl in the presence of 10 mol% FeCl 3 in CH 2Cl2 at
30 1C. The reaction reached completion within 1 h and delivered
a product in a good yield. To our surprise, cyclopentene product
3a was obtained instead of 2-type cyclohexene based on the
1Ha n d 13C spectra of the product. Then attention was paid to
the optimization of the reaction conditions for this transforma-
tion. It was found that the reaction could not proceed to aﬀord
the product 3a in most of the tested solvents, such as CH
3CN,
DCE, THF, DMF, DMSO, CH 3NO2, dioxane, 1,1,1-trichloro-
ethane or 1,1,2-trichloroethane (Table S1, entries 2–10, ESI w).
Dichloromethane was found to be the best solvent (Table S1,
entry 1, ESIw).
Next, various Lewis acids were examined in this reaction
(Table 1). Cyclopropane 1a was found to be successfully
converted to 3a in moderate to good yields in the presence
of Lewis acids,
13 such as FeCl 3, Sc(OTf) 3, Zn(OTf) 2, AgOTf,
Cu(OTf)2, or ZnCl 2 (Table 1, entries 1–6). Of these Zn(OTf) 2

gave the best result, aﬀording 3a in 81% yield. In contrast,
TiCl4 or BF 3/C1Et2O13 could not lead to the formation of 3a
(Table 1, entries 7 and 8). Interestingly, reducing the catalyst
loading of Zn(OTf)
2 from 10 mol% to 5 mol% improved the
yield of 3a from 84% to 94% within 2 h (Table 1, entry 9). No
product was obtained either in the absence of a Lewis acid
(Table 1, entry 10) or TMSCl (Table 1, entry 11). Thus, we
deﬁned the reaction of 1 equiv. 1 and 1.2 equiv. TMSCl
catalyzed by 5 mol% Zn(OTf)
2 in CH 2Cl2 at 30 1C as the
standard conditions.
With the optimized protocol in hand, we turned to demonstrate
the generality of this reaction. The results summarized in Table 2
show that this reaction indeed provides a straightforward entry to
a variety of cyclopentene derivatives in moderate to good yields.
Diﬀerent substitutions at the terminal position of allene, such as
methyl, ethyl, cyclohexyl and cyclopentyl could be accommo-
dated in the reaction, aﬀording the corresponding cyclopentenes
3a–3n in good yields (Table 2). Dimethyl, diethyl, and dibenzyl
malonates are all proper substrates for this reaction, aﬀording the
corresponding products in moderate to good yields. Alkyl, benzyl,
and allyl substituted 1,3,4-alkatrien-2-ylcyclopropanes proceeded
smoothly to aﬀord the corresponding products3a–3nin moderate
to good yields. When 1.7 g of 1a (4.7 mmol) was used, 3a was
obtained in 83% yield.
Product 3l was treated with sodium hydroxide (2 M aqueous
solution) in ethanol at 60 1C for 1 hour, followed by quenching
with hydrochloride to aﬀord a solid product 4 in 94% isolated
yield (Scheme 2). Thus, the structure of 3 was then further
conﬁrmed unambiguously by the X-ray diﬀraction study of 4
(Scheme 2).
14
A rationale is proposed as shown in Scheme 3. Initially,
cyclopropane is activated by the chelation of Lewis acids to
the carbonyl groups of the ester groups to polarize the
cyclopropanyl ring. Then ring-opening occurred to aﬀord
1,3-zwitterionic intermediate B. The substituted group at the
2-position of 1,3,4-alkatrien-2-yl cyclopropane was essential to
the ring-opening process of cyclopropylvinylallenes since the
reaction was completely shut down when R
2 was a proton,
probably due to the instability of the carbocation after ring-
opening reaction. Then nucleophile X
/C0 attacks the central
carbon atom of the allene moiety, which is followed by
intramolecular cyclopropanation to form intermediate C with
a cyclopropanylmethylene unit. The carbon anion center in
intermediate C attacks the three-membered ring to form
cyclopentane intermediate D, which is in resonance with
intermediate E. Finally, intermediate E is quenched by a
proton from the environment to aﬀord the product 3 while
regenerating the Lewis acid catalyst.
In summary, we have developed a unique ring-opening/
cyclization of cyclopropylvinylallenes with TMSX in the
presence of a Lewis acid, which provides a straightforward
